visual.general_description: Axial contrast-enhanced chest CT image with two arrows.
visual.detailed_description: One axial CT slice through the upper chest in a soft-tissue window with intravenous contrast opacification: bright contrast-filled mediastinal vessels including a large rounded structure and a branching vessel extending toward the left of the image, the airways dark, and two lungs with small vessels. Two thin arrows are drawn on the image, a yellow arrow pointing at a slightly darker region beside the bright central vessels on the left of the image and a white arrow pointing at the end of a bright branching vessel on the right of the image. No printed text, numbers, scale bars, patient names, dates or device text are visible; the image is cropped to the chest and shows no face; a few bright dots at the top edge lie outside the body outline. The identity of the vessels, the nature of the filling defects and image laterality are not judged from pixels; they are caption claims.

Biopsies were taken and histology showed partial villous atrophy (villous : crypt ratio 1 : 3) with crypt hyperplasia and a marked increase in intraepithelial lymphocytes (80 lymphocytes per 100 epithelial cells) consistent with celiac sprue, Marsh classification 3B (Figures 2 and 3).
